common_mode_conclusion: gap spread across cells = 0.00965 vs mean |mu| = 0.0406; a common-mode gap (small spread relative to the paired-delta scale) largely CANCELS in the paired ΔIR(4-5) and ΔIR(4-2) deltas; a per-cell-heterogeneous gap does not.
estimator_stated: per-step mean-field decode_latent(E[z]) along a GREEDY argmax token path; exact only under a linear decoder in z + deterministic path; mc_mean = unbiased-in-expectation MC reference
key_diagnostic: On the ACCEPTANCE cell4, expectation gives BALANCED frac_neg=0.5 (matching mc_mean) — so the money-leg cell4 frac_neg=0.999 (mostly-short) is a MODEL property of that specific 3000-step cell, NOT an estimator artifact. Because training is SIGMA-invariant, the re-run reproduces that cell4 bit-identically (sign pattern fixed), so raising SIGMA cannot correct its sign bias.
positions_robustness_finding: The gap is directionally COMMON-MODE (both cells +0.023..+0.032) and a LEVEL shift, NOT a sign shift: frac_neg is IDENTICAL between expectation and mc_mean for each cell (cell4 0.5=0.5, cell2 0.0=0.0). Since positions come from sign(mu) gated by |mu|>k*c, a level shift that preserves the sign distribution preserves POSITIONS (hence IR), so the paired DIR clauses are robust to it; the only residual channel is marginal decisions near +/-k*c. mc_mean (unbiased) remains the reference; expectation understates the negative drift by ~+0.025..+0.032 (a delta-method level bias) without flipping signs.
